quick.summary: The best way to organize a cluttered settings menu so people can navigate easily.
quick.takeaway: Group items by what the person is trying to achieve, not by system limits.

beats.line: Our settings menu has twenty links. How do I sort them out?
Think of a tea stall. They do not list every single leaf.
They offer black tea, green tea, and herbal tea.
So I should group the settings into a few main buckets.
Yes. This reduces their cognitive load.
Can I just say it makes it easier to think?
I like that better. Less thinking is good.
Group things by what the person is trying to achieve.
Like putting passwords and privacy under an account security label.
That is it. Name the buckets for the user.

quiz.question: You have twenty features to organize. How should you group them?
options: By the task the person wants to complete.
By the internal team that built them.
By the color of their icons.
quiz.explanation: Organizing by user goals reduces the amount of thinking required to find things quickly.

quiz.question: Showing every single option at once makes navigation easier for the user.
quiz.explanation: Too many choices create a heavy cognitive load. Grouping them into broad categories makes it easier to think.
